title: Mathematics avoids undecidability by choosing questions its methods can answer

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Mathematics avoids undecidability by choosing questions its methods can answer

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Undecidability and unprovability have seemed rare in mathematics because mathematics, shaped by its history, has defined itself around the questions and systems that proof-based methods can address, concentrating on limited patches of computational reducibility; so present-day mathematics is a small and uncharacteristic sample of what is possible.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is that like most other fields of human inquiry mathematics has tended to define itself to be concerned with just those questions that its methods can successfully address.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Implications for Mathematics and Its Foundations” (from p. 772), p. 792. Scope: the practice and history of mathematics

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-38: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public mathematical corpora can document selection patterns but cannot resolve the claimed causal explanation or whether present mathematics is uncharacteristic of all possibilities. The central comparison lacks a measurable reference population.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Historical and bibliometric studies could compare researched topics with known decidability and tractability, but cannot observe the counterfactual universe of possible mathematics or isolate methodological self-selection as the cause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Known undecidability is itself affected by research attention.

The population of possible mathematics is undefined.

Historical selection and technical tractability are mutually entangled.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sentence is a historical thesis: mathematics selected questions its proof methods can answer, so the present subject is a small uncharacteristic sample of what is possible. Classification databases record what was studied. They do not record why alternatives were set aside, and they do not encode the space of possible systems, so rival histories fit the same record.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare questions mathematicians emphasize with a neutral sample of questions about simple formal systems, and test whether the emphasized set is the decidable subset. The claim provides neither the sample nor a measure of emphasis.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The same publication record fits difficulty, taste, and applicability as causes.

Defined itself to avoid encodes an intention that publication records omit.

An uncharacteristic sample needs a measure on all possible mathematics.
